The model rests on a few rules:
A person is a separate user in every scope they sign in to.
A login authenticates only its own scope's users.
Credentials are stored apart from users and never leave the server.
Each sign-in provider belongs to exactly one login, and its owner can never reach anything of the system's.
There are three scopes, each with its own kind of user:
— a user of one application, in one of its tenants

Three scopes rather than two, because they are real trust boundaries:
An organization's developers should not automatically be users of every application they build.
An application's users should not reach the organization's tooling.
Applications of one organization can serve unrelated user populations.

It is refused on an organization's configuration — organizations add their members — and it creates a user only where that user gets a tenant: at an application's login while the system manages its tenants, or at a tenant's login through the tenant's own configuration. A configuration that admits every Microsoft directory creates a user only under an email the token proves (

A user an administrator added is claimed by its first sign-in through a provider of its own login under the same email; at an organization, only through the organization's own provider. After that, only the binding identifies the user.

An organization never enters a URL. It picks a provider type and gives its account there (an Entra directory id, an Okta domain); the server fills the type's issuer template on every save, and account patterns admit no scheme, port, path or foreign host. So every host the server fetches belongs to the provider. Identity endpoints are fetched without following redirects, and the deployment's egress policy blocks the node's metadata addresses.

No secret is stored on a configuration row. A system registration's secret is fetched from the system's secret storage at sign-in time. An organization's secret is given on save, stored in the organization's own scope keyed by the configuration, and never read back through any service;
only says whether one is held. A save without a secret keeps the one held.
Organization sign-up always founds a new organization with the founder as its first user, whatever other organizations the person belongs to. People join an existing organization only by being added.
